root: ^This is your first week of internship at the Science Div.
^The past few days, you've been busy familiarizing yourself with the environment and learning about each department's responsibilities.
^Your previous mentor was always rushing around and barely supervised you.
^You're standing in the hallway, looking at your tablet, when a new notification arrives.
^Your new mentor is Dr. L. Ye. Please report to the Chief Advisor's office by 12 P.M."
^Ecology Department Greenhouse, Chief Advisor's Office · 12 P.M.
^You knock on the door. No answer.
^You push it open to find a somewhat cluttered office. The desk is piled with plant samples, data tablets, and several oddly-growing potted plants.
^You see someone emerge from the storage room, arms full of equipment.
^Lin: Oh, you're here. Sorry about the mess.
^You watch her set the items down and shake your hand.
^Lin: I'm Lin, Chief Advisor of Ecology Department. You should have seen the assignment notice.
^Lin: Your previous mentor was transferred. I'll be overseeing your internship from now on.
^She pours you a cup of tea.
^Lin: The internship work is straightforward—you'll assist me with routine projects during the day, organize data, tend to experimental plants.
^Lin: Most of the time it'll be pretty boring. Watering, recording, writing reports.
^Lin: By the way, are you interested in ecological modeling?
^You see her pull up a holographic projection—green lines and data flowing densely across the display.
^Lin: This is an ecological simulation system.
^Lin: The Academy is preparing a long-term project that requires testing the stability of various plant combinations in ecosystems.
^Lin: I'm responsible for technical support and data analysis, but to be honest...
^She tucks a strand of hair behind her ear.
^Lin: Running simulation tests... I really don't have that much time for it.
^Lin: So if you're willing, I could hand this part over to you.
^Lin: The operation isn't difficult—select plants, adjust environmental parameters, observe the system running, record data.
^Lin: Consider it one of your internship projects. What do you say?
